ErrorBody.description:
The error envelope every daemon error and every client side IPC error
uses (VAL-020).

`code`, `category`, `message`, `retryable`, and `details` are frozen
across majors, so peers of any major can always exchange
`protocol.major_mismatch`.

category.description: The category the catalog gives the code.

details.description: Extra facts, with keys only from the code's catalog entry.

fields.description: The params fields that failed, for `request.invalid_params`.

hint.description: A safe recovery step, in English.

items.description:
A structured list that does not fit in `details`, with the item
`kind` and field keys from the code's catalog entry.

message.description:
One safe English sentence: lowercase start, no trailing period, at
most 200 characters, never a secret.

retryable.description:
True only when the daemon guarantees the request had no effect, so
the exact same request may be sent again.

rule.description: The PRD rule ID behind the error, such as `BR-008`.

ErrorCategory.description:
What a client should do about an error. Closed: a new category is a new
protocol major. Feature 8 derives CLI exit codes from it.

oneOf.description: Fix the input; sending the same request again fails again.
The resource does not exist; refresh the snapshot.
State changed or the resource is in use; refresh, then decide.
Identity, peer, or trust was refused; never retry on its own.
The version, method, or capability is not supported.
The daemon or a dependency is not available yet; check `retryable`.
The work ran and failed.
A time limit passed; the outcome may be unknown, check the operation.
The work was cancelled.
A bug or a broken invariant in Stackly.

ErrorDetail.description: One extra fact on an error, as a key and a string value.

key.description: A camelCase key from the code's catalog entry.

requestId.description:
The request that failed, or null only when its `requestId` could not
be read.

ErrorItem.description:
One entry of a structured list on an error, such as one reference that
needs a secret (spec 0011) or one manifest issue (spec 0009).

`kind` and the field keys are plain strings, so a client always decodes
an error frame, even with an item kind it does not know yet.

fields.description: The item's facts, with keys from the code's catalog entry.

kind.description: The item kind from the code's catalog entry, such as `issue`.

resource.description: The resource the event is about.

revision.description: The resource's revision after the change.

sequence.description: Position in this daemon run, rising by one per published event.

subscriptionId.description: The subscription this event is delivered for.

EventCursor.description: A position in the event stream of one daemon run.

sequence.description: The last sequence seen; 0 means no event yet.

serverInstanceId.description: The daemon run the sequence belongs to.

EventKind.description:
What happened. Each kind is `<area>.<name>`; the owner of an area adds
its kinds here. Clients skip kinds they do not know through
[`EventProbe`], so a new kind is a minor bump.

oneOf.description: The subscriber missed events; take a new snapshot.
The daemon is shutting down.

An operation was created or changed state (spec 0007). The event's
resource is the operation and its revision the operation's.

An operation changed without changing state: stage, progress,
`waitingOn`, the point of no return, or a cancel (spec 0007).

FieldError.description:
One params field that failed to decode or validate. An error carries at
most 32 of them (`FIELD_ERRORS_MAX`) and counts the rest in its
`omitted` detail.

code.description: A code from the fixed set in [`FieldCode`].

message.description: The fixed text of the code; never the input value.

path.description:
Where the field sits, relative to the params, such as `name`,
`since.sequence`, or `kinds[3]`. At most 256 characters.

GapReason.description: Why a subscriber missed events. Open: newer daemons may add values.

oneOf.description: The subscriber fell more than the event buffer behind.
The cursor is older than the replay ring.
The cursor belongs to another daemon run.
A reason this build does not know. The daemon never sends it.

HandshakeAccepted.description:
Reply of `daemon.handshake` when the majors match and the params are
valid.

contractDrift.description:
True when the versions match but the digests differ: the connection
works, and the daemon logs one warning.

head.description:
The newest event cursor at handshake time; sequence 0 means no event
yet.

protocol.description: The protocol version the daemon speaks.

serverInstanceId.description: A fresh UUID v7 for each daemon run; event cursors belong to it.

InstallVerdict.description: The install gate's verdict for one version on this Mac.

installable.description: Whether the version can be installed.

reason.description: Why not; null when it can.

Limits.description: The limits a daemon enforces, as sent in `HandshakeAccepted`.

eventBufferLen.description: Events a subscriber may fall behind before an overflow gap.

maxFrameBytes.description: Largest control frame payload, in bytes.

maxInFlightRequests.description: Most requests in flight per connection.

maxLogBatchBytes.description: Largest log batch payload, in bytes.

Reply of `catalog.list_providers`: every entry in display order, in one
page.

items.description:
Provider and invalid entries first, planned entries last; then
category, display name, and ID.

created.description: What it created or claimed, in order.

OperationFailureInfo.description: Why an operation failed; only in state `failed`.

error.description: The error that ended the operation, with `operationId` set.

reason.description:
The engine's reason code, such as `step_failed`, `interrupted`, or
`abandoned`.

retryable.description:
True when a new operation with a new idempotency key may succeed.
It differs from `error.retryable`, which is about sending the same
request again.

OperationKind.description:
What an operation does: the kind codes of spec 0004. Open: a newer
daemon may add kinds, which older clients read as `unrecognized`.

next.description:
The cursor of the next page, to send back as `before`; null on the
last page.

OperationProgress.description: How far an operation got. Closed.

oneOf.description: The work does not know how much is left.

partial.description:
The items that did not all go to plan; a client shows the operation
as partial when this is not empty.

resources.description: The resources the operation created or changed.

OperationState.description:
The state of an operation (PRD section 18.2). Closed: a new state is a
new protocol major.

oneOf.description: Waiting to run, either new or resumed.
Running.

Finished with success; final.

autoCompensatedAtStart.description: Operations the daemon undid on its own when it started.

interruptedAtStart.description: Operations the daemon found interrupted when it started.

maxQueued.description: The most operations that wait in the queue.

maxRunning.description: The most operations that run at once.

rejectedQueueFull.description:
Requests refused with `operation.queue_full` since the daemon

resumedAtStart.description: Operations the daemon resumed on its own when it started.

OperationStepInfo.description:
One step of an operation's journal. The step's checkpoint is never
sent.

attempts.description: How many times the step started, at least 1.

errorCode.description: The catalog code of the step's failure; only in state `failed`.

finishedAt.description: When the step ended; null while it runs.

repeatable.description: Whether the engine may run the step again after an interruption.

reversible.description: Whether the engine can undo the step.

OperationSummary.description:
One operation as every client sees it, in replies and in both
operation events.

cancelRequestedAt.description: When a cancel was asked for.

failure.description: Why the operation failed; only in state `failed`.

id.description: The operation ID, a lowercase UUID v7.

pointOfNoReturnAt.description:
When the first step that cannot be undone started. From then on a
cancel no longer stops the work.

recovery.description: What needs the person's action; only in state `needs_recovery`.

resource.description:
The resource the operation works on; null for `update_manager`
before it names the manager.

result.description: What the operation produced, once it ended or was abandoned.

revision.description: The operation's revision; every committed change raises it.

stage.description: What the operation is doing now, such as `downloading`.

startedAt.description: When the operation first started running.

state.description: The state, one of the seven of PRD section 18.2.

waitingOn.description:
The operation this one waits for while queued: the oldest one that
holds or waits for one of its locks.

client.description: The kind of client that sent the request; null for the daemon.

origin.description: A request, or the daemon itself.

PartialItem.description: One item of a partial result, such as one leftover of an abandon.

code.description: A catalog code that explains the outcome, if any.

item.description: What the item is, such as a created item's reference.

resource.description: The resource the item belongs to, if any.

PartialOutcome.description: What happened to one item of a partial result. Open.

oneOf.description: Done, or cleaned up.

ProtocolVersion.description:
Version of the IPC protocol a peer speaks.

`major` changes when the wire breaks, `minor` when it only gains optional
additions. Peers with the same major always talk, whatever their minors.

major.description: Bumped for every breaking change to the wire.
